newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sydkraft sees better result in '97.
newsitem.headline: Sydkraft sees better result in '97.

text.p: Swedish power company Sydkraft forecast on Monday that its 1997 result would be better than last year's earnings, excluding a one-off gain from the sale of shares in German group VEBA.
The sale of VEBA shares will boost the result by 2.2 billion crowns, the company said in a statement.
The company reduced its stake in VEBA to one percent from 3.2 percent earlier this year.
"1997 has begun warmer than usual, which has meant lower electricity sales compared to last year when it was very cold," chief executive Goran Ahlstrom said in the company's annual report.
"At the same time there has been much precipitation, both rain and snow, which means reservoirs are filling up."
Currently, water levels are only slightly lower than normal, he said. Levels were extremely low this winter.
